maria: Heads up — eval-runner broke during the quant-int8 model bring-up. BLEU numbers are insane compared to baseline, and BERTScore sometimes returns NaN. Posting the failing command + a short log excerpt.

maria: ```
$ pytest tests/evals/test_metrics_smoke.py::test_bleu_pipeline -k quant
E   AssertionError: BLEU diff > 0.15 (0.47 vs 0.02)
...
IndexError: token id out of vocab (at batch collate)
```

aj: Did this start after the tokenizer refactor? I merged the fast-tokenizer PR (#472) yesterday afternoon. Might be a compat issue with pad/truncation semantics. :thinking_face:

sanjay: Can you paste the runner config? I suspect the collate function is still doing pad_to_length=True which the new tokenizer doesn't expose, so sequences get truncated differently and BLEU/ROUGE get skewed. Also if detokenization yields empty strings, BERTScore returns NaN.

maria: Runner config snippet and offending line:```yaml
runner:
  batch_size: 8
  collate_fn: default_collate
  tokenizer: fast-tokenizer
  pad_to_length: true
```
Log: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "eval_runner.py", line 214, in run_batch
    ids = tokenizer(batch[text_key], pad_to_length=True)
IndexError: token id out of vocab

WARNING: 10 predictions were empty after detokenization -> BERTScore=NaN
```

eileen: Two things to tackle: (1) runner collate + tokenizer API mismatch — change collate to use tokenizer.pad or tokenizer(..., padding='longest') rather than forcing pad_to_length. (2) Metric guards: our BERTScore wrapper should skip empty preds and log count; BLEU should normalize/strip and fallback to corpus-level smoothing if a sample is empty. Quick patch example: ```python
# metrics/bertscore_wrapper.py
def safe_bertscore(preds, refs):
  preds = [p if p.strip() else "<empty>" for p in preds]
  return bertscore.score(preds, refs, model_type="roberta-large")
```
And add an assert in the metric harness to fail on NaN/inf.

aj: I'll revert the tokenizer change on main for now and push a fix for the collate in a follow-up. Also noticed pass@k is double-counting when we dedupe candidates before scoring — the pass@k impl expects original candidate set size. Quick fix: compute pass@k on deduped lists or keep track of original counts. Proposed snippet:```python
# evals/pass_at_k.py
def pass_at_k(candidates, k):
  unique = list(dict.fromkeys(candidates))  # preserves order, dedup
  n = len(unique)
  # compute pass@k using n, not len(candidates)
```

sanjay: CI note: the smoke test on macOS runner is flaky due to tokenizer wheel differences. We should pin the tokenizer package version in the evals Dockerfile and add a small CI test that asserts metrics are finite (no NaN/inf) and BLEU/ROUGE within a plausible range vs a stored baseline. That will catch regressions like this before merge.

ci-bot: CI: re-run triggered for eng-ml/evals (pipeline #1845674329). Previous run failed: eval-smoke-metrics. Re-running now.

eileen: I'll open a tiny PR with these fixes: guard empty preds, BLEU normalization, pass@k dedupe handling, and a unit test for quant:int8 model output shapes + metrics. Assigning tokenizer revert + CI pin to @aj. Thanks — will add changelog entry in docs/evals/notes.md :white_check_mark:
